questions.question: What type of raw material is traditional plastic food packaging usually made from?
options: Renewable biological resources
Non-renewable fossil fuels
Recycled plant fibers
Synthetic mineral ores

questions.question: Why is plastic waste in landfill sites and oceans considered a major environmental concern?
options: It breaks down completely within days without harming wildlife
It absorbs excess carbon dioxide directly from ocean waters
It persists for a long time without degrading and harms living organisms
It dissolves instantly and increases soil acidity levels

questions.question: Why are biodegradable bioplastics considered a sustainable alternative to traditional plastics?
options: They are made from renewable resources and break down naturally
They are produced directly from crude oil with zero carbon emissions
They never degrade, making them permanent storage containers
They require no land or energy to manufacture

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of using plastic packaging for food items?
options: It completely eliminates the need for farming
It helps prevent food spoilage and reduces overall food waste
It permanently lowers global atmospheric temperatures
It absorbs greenhouse gases directly from the kitchen air

questions.question: Why does food production require large amounts of land?
options: Plants can only grow in artificially built greenhouse structures
Growing crops to feed humans and livestock occupies vast areas of land
Farmland must be left completely covered in concrete to protect soil
Animal farming requires no land compared to crop farming

questions.question: What is one of the primary reasons forests are cleared worldwide (deforestation)?
options: Building underground transport tunnels
Converting land for agricultural use and farming
Storing excess rainwater in open reservoirs
Creating natural wildlife reserves

questions.question: How does deforestation directly affect wild organisms living in forests?
options: It leads to habitat loss for many different species
It increases the size of their natural habitats
It protects them from extreme weather conditions
It provides extra food sources for all forest animals

questions.question: Which option represents a positive land use change used as a climate change mitigation strategy?
options: Expanding urban concrete developments
Reforestation and rewilding of land
Clearing native woodland for palm oil crops
Draining natural wetlands for cattle farming

questions.question: How does climate change make food production more challenging?
options: By reducing the overall carbon footprint of all crops to zero
By making extreme weather events more frequent and intense
By completely preventing pests from attacking food crops
By keeping global temperatures completely constant year-round

questions.question: What contributes to the total carbon footprint of a food product?
options: Only the distance the food travels after purchase
Emissions of greenhouse gases at various stages of production
Only the oxygen consumed by plants during respiration
The weight of the packaging material alone

questions.question: How can changing human dietary choices help combat climate change?
options: It causes an immediate increase in atmospheric methane
It lowers greenhouse gas emissions associated with food production
It stops the natural water cycle from functioning
It removes the need for photosynthesis in agricultural crops

questions.question: What is the main benefit of comparing greenhouse gas emissions data for different diets?
options: It guarantees that all food prices will immediately drop
It helps us evaluate the environmental impact of our food choices
It reveals which foods contain the highest amounts of minerals
It eliminates the need for agricultural land worldwide

questions.question: How does deforestation disrupt the global carbon cycle?
options: Less carbon dioxide is absorbed from the atmosphere because photosynthesis is reduced
More carbon dioxide is absorbed by tree roots in cleared areas
Photosynthesis increases dramatically in cleared pasture land
Trees release pure oxygen that traps heat in the atmosphere

questions.question: What role does carbon dioxide play in climate change?
options: It acts as a cooling agent that lowers Earth average temperature
It is a greenhouse gas that enhances the greenhouse effect, trapping heat
It blocks sunlight from entering the Earth upper atmosphere completely
It destroys water vapor in the atmosphere, causing dry air worldwide

questions.question: In what way does deforestation affect the local water cycle?
options: It increases the rate of plant transpiration into the air
Less water is absorbed by tree roots and transpired into the atmosphere
It prevents all rainfall from reaching the forest floor
It converts all atmospheric groundwater directly into ice

questions.question: What is a consequence of increased surface runoff caused by deforestation?
options: Reduced risk of river flooding in agricultural areas
Increased flooding and potential threats to food security
Complete protection of topsoil from water erosion
Lower sea levels in surrounding coastal regions

questions.question: Which strategy helps prevent further deforestation and protects forest ecosystems?
options: Removing legal restrictions on timber harvesting
Implementing legal protection for forests and planting new trees
Subsidizing the burning of woodland for crop expansion
Replacing wild forests with single-crop agricultural fields

questions.question: What is the primary cause of modern global warming and climate change?
options: Natural solar fluctuations alone
Human emissions of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere
A decrease in global agricultural activity
Increased absorption of heat by polar ice caps

questions.question: How does climate change affect species living in specific habitats?
options: It improves habitat conditions for all existing species equally
It alters habitat conditions, making species less adapted to their environment
It prevents any changes in local temperatures or rainfall patterns
It instantly gives species new physical features to survive higher heat

questions.question: What can be a direct impact of more frequent extreme weather events caused by climate change?
options: An overall increase in global biodiversity
Loss of biodiversity as species fail to survive severe events
Complete stabilization of all natural ecosystems
The total end of natural selection in affected habitats
